database_summary: This is a Formula 1 racing results schema (SQLite) with descriptive dimension-like tables for circuits, constructors, drivers, seasons and status; event/race header table (races); and multiple fact/event/detail tables capturing results, standings, lap times, pit stops, qualifying and constructor-related outcomes. Row counts indicate a historic multi-season dataset (seasons 68 rows, races 976, lapTimes 420k). Most tables record event-level or session-level facts (results, lapTimes, pitStops, qualifying, constructorResults, driverStandings, constructorStandings).

accepted.name: race_basic
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  raceId,
  year,
  round,
  circuitId,
  name,
  date,
  time,
  -- combine date and time when both present; NULL if time missing
  CASE
    WHEN date IS NOT NULL AND time IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(time) != '' THEN date || ' ' || time
    WHEN date IS NOT NULL THEN date
    ELSE NULL
  END AS datetime
FROM races
accepted.description: Normalized race header rows with explicit datetime and preserved race identifiers. Use this to join event/date info to results, standings, lap times, qualifying, etc. | Use for: List races in a season or between dates; Join race metadata to results/qualifying/standings; Filter events by circuit, round, or date/time

accepted.name: driver_dim
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  driverId,
  driverRef,
  number,
  code,
  forename,
  surname,
  dob,
  nationality,
  url
FROM drivers
accepted.description: Canonical driver dimension exposing identity and birth date/nationality for joins and demographic filtering. | Use for: Find drivers by nationality or birth year; Join driver names to results, lapTimes, pitStops, qualifying

accepted.name: constructor_dim
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  constructorId,
  constructorRef,
  name,
  nationality,
  url
FROM constructors
accepted.description: Constructor/team dimension for joins and grouping in performance queries. | Use for: Aggregate points by constructor; List constructors by nationality; Join constructor attributes to results/standings

accepted.name: race_results_enriched
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  r.resultId,
  r.raceId,
  r.driverId,
  r.constructorId,
  r.number,
  r.grid,
  r.position,
  r.positionText,
  r.positionOrder,
  r.points,
  r.laps,
  r.time,
  r.milliseconds,
  r.fastestLap,
  r.rank AS rank,
  r.fastestLapTime,
  r.fastestLapSpeed,
  r.statusId,
  ra.year,
  ra.round,
  ra.circuitId,
  ra.name AS name,
  ra.date,
  ra.time AS time_of_race,
  d.forename,
  d.surname,
  d.code,
  d.number AS driver_number,
  d.nationality AS driver_nationality,
  c.name AS constructor_name,
  c.nationality AS constructor_nationality,
  s.status AS status
FROM results r
LEFT JOIN races ra ON r.raceId = ra.raceId
LEFT JOIN drivers d ON r.driverId = d.driverId
LEFT JOIN constructors c ON r.constructorId = c.constructorId
LEFT JOIN status s ON r.statusId = s.statusId
grain: resultId (one row per race result entry)
accepted.description: Denormalized results rows joined to races, drivers and constructors. Useful as a single wide table for filtering, aggregations, and ranking across race results. | Use for: Compare driver/constructor performance in a race or season; Filter results by position, points, status; Build leaderboards or time-based analyses using result milliseconds

accepted.name: driver_lap_aggregates
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  raceId,
  driverId,
  COUNT(*) AS lap_count,
  MIN(milliseconds) AS best_lap_ms,
  MAX(milliseconds) AS worst_lap_ms,
  AVG(milliseconds) AS avg_lap_ms
FROM lapTimes
GROUP BY raceId, driverId
accepted.description: Aggregated lap-time measures per driver per race (count, best/worst/avg milliseconds). Useful for comparing consistency and pace within a race or across races. | Use for: Find fastest lap per driver in a race; Compare average lap times between drivers or races; Detect drivers with missing lap records (lap_count smaller than expected)

accepted.name: pitstop_aggregates
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  raceId,
  driverId,
  COUNT(*) AS pit_count,
  SUM(milliseconds) AS total_pit_ms,
  AVG(milliseconds) AS avg_pit_ms
FROM pitStops
GROUP BY raceId, driverId
accepted.description: Aggregated pit stop metrics per driver per race (count, total/avg milliseconds). Useful to analyze pit strategy and time lost in pits. | Use for: Compare pit stop frequency and total pit time between drivers; Correlate pit stop time with race position changes

accepted.name: season_driver_points
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  r.year,
  res.driverId,
  SUM(res.points) AS season_points,
  COUNT(DISTINCT res.raceId) AS races_participated
FROM results res
JOIN races r ON res.raceId = r.raceId
GROUP BY r.year, res.driverId
accepted.description: Total points per driver per season (year), aggregating results.points across races. Useful for season-level leaderboards and trend analysis. | Use for: Rank drivers by season points; Compute points per race averages; Filter drivers who participated in at least N races (post-filter)

accepted.name: season_constructor_points
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  r.year,
  res.constructorId,
  SUM(res.points) AS season_points,
  COUNT(DISTINCT res.raceId) AS races_participated
FROM results res
JOIN races r ON res.raceId = r.raceId
GROUP BY r.year, res.constructorId
accepted.description: Total points per constructor per season (year), aggregating results.points across races. Useful for constructor championship analyses. | Use for: Rank constructors by season points; Analyze constructor participation across seasons

accepted.name: driver_season_rank
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  sp.year,
  sp.driverId,
  sp.season_points,
  sp.races_participated,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY sp.year ORDER BY sp.season_points DESC) AS season_rank
FROM (
  SELECT
    r.year,
    res.driverId,
    SUM(res.points) AS season_points,
    COUNT(DISTINCT res.raceId) AS races_participated
  FROM results res
  JOIN races r ON res.raceId = r.raceId
  GROUP BY r.year, res.driverId
) sp
grain: year, driverId (one row per driver per season with rank)
accepted.description: Season ranking of drivers by season points with ties handled by RANK(); outputs rank per driver per year. Use this to select top-K drivers per season by filtering on rank. | Use for: Top-K drivers per season; Track rank progression across seasons (join by driverId)

accepted.name: fastest_lap_per_race
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  lt_min.raceId,
  lt_min.best_lap_ms,
  lt.driverId,
  lt.lap,
  lt.time AS time,
  lt.position
FROM (
  SELECT raceId, MIN(milliseconds) AS best_lap_ms
  FROM lapTimes
  GROUP BY raceId
) lt_min
JOIN lapTimes lt
  ON lt.raceId = lt_min.raceId
  AND lt.milliseconds = lt_min.best_lap_ms
grain: raceId, driverId, lap (one row per driver lap matching the race fastest lap; may be multiple if tie)
accepted.description: Fastest lap (minimum milliseconds) per race with driver(s) who set it. Useful to find the single best lap in each race and associated drivers. | Use for: Who set the fastest lap in each race; Compare fastest lap times across races or drivers

accepted.name: qualifying_grid_positions
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  q.qualifyId,
  q.raceId,
  q.driverId,
  q.constructorId,
  q.number,
  q.position AS qual_position,
  q.q1,
  q.q2,
  q.q3,
  ra.year,
  ra.round,
  ra.circuitId,
  d.forename,
  d.surname,
  c.name AS constructor_name
FROM qualifying q
LEFT JOIN races ra ON q.raceId = ra.raceId
LEFT JOIN drivers d ON q.driverId = d.driverId
LEFT JOIN constructors c ON q.constructorId = c.constructorId
accepted.description: Qualifying positions joined to race and driver info, exposing final qualifying position and Q1/Q2/Q3 times for grid analyses. | Use for: Compare qualifying position to race results; Analyze Q1/Q2/Q3 performance per driver or circuit

accepted.name: driver_running_points_by_season
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  sp.year,
  sp.driverId,
  sp.raceId,
  sp.race_date,
  sp.points_in_race,
  SUM(sp.points_in_race) OVER (PARTITION BY sp.year, sp.driverId ORDER BY sp.race_date, sp.raceId ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS running_season_points
FROM (
  SELECT
    r.year,
    res.driverId,
    res.raceId,
    r.date AS race_date,
    SUM(res.points) AS points_in_race
  FROM results res
  JOIN races r ON res.raceId = r.raceId
  GROUP BY r.year, res.driverId, res.raceId, r.date
) sp
grain: year, driverId, raceId (one row per driver per race with cumulative season points up to that race)
accepted.description: Cumulative running total of points per driver within each season ordered by race date (uses raceId order via date). Useful to plot championship progression race-by-race. | Use for: Plot championship points progression for a driver in a season; Determine points lead after each race
